inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 242m ordinary shares outstanding at 31 August 2026 (Sep-2026 corporate presentation, p.4) plus 5.3m potential dilutive PSUs (FY2025 AR note 7F: 241.3m basic -> 246.6m total potential diluted). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. The count IS being funded -- $87.4m FY2025 and $71m H1-2026 of buybacks cancel roughly the PSU issuance.
inputs.net_debt_basis: 30 June 2026 (H1-2026 results presentation p.11 and Sep-2026 presentation p.46): cash $1,252m less $500m 7% Senior Notes due Oct-2030, $410m drawn RCF and $88m Lafigue term loan = net cash $254m. Lease liabilities (~$90m) are EXCLUDED because lease payments are charged inside the flows (treatment B). The RCF was repaid after quarter-end, which does not change net debt. Dec-2025 net debt was ~$160m ex-leases; the $414m swing to June is H1-2026 FCF ($761m) less $301m shareholder returns and other items. Y1 (FY2026) flows are modelled for the full year, so H1-2026 FCF is in both the anchor and Y1 -- worth roughly $1.7/share -- but the engine also discounts Y1 by a full year from a notional 1-Jan-2026 start when the valuation is dated October, which understates value by ~8%; the net bias is conservative and is left as the folder convention.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report consolidated cash flow note 21A 'Share-based compensation 64.7' (FY2024: 21.4), which already includes the fair-value movement on cash-settled DSUs; the $3.0m cash paid on DSU/PSU settlement is inside that expense and is NOT added again. FY2025 SBC was inflated by the 171% share price rise (reserve-only equity-settled charge was $53.5m); H1-2026 ran $23m, so the forward path anchors at 1.2% of revenue.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income $6.5m (AR p.8834). Not stripped: net cash ($254m) is well below 1x the FCF base, so the cash pile is not material enough to double count.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in USD; LSE quote in GBp (pence). GBPUSD 1.3233 at 2026-10-09T21:29Z (Yahoo GBPUSD=X), so 1 USD = 75.57 GBp (model -> quote). Parity check against the TSX line: EDV.TO C$77.35 (2026-10-09 close) / USDCAD 1.4254 = US$54.27 vs LSE 4,126p / 75.57 = US$54.60, a 0.6% tie (different closing times). Unsuffixed per-share values are in GBp to match current_price; USD twins are the engine's native output.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the currency of the flows: 10-year UST 5.24% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-10-09) rounded to 5.2%, beta 1.0 (senior gold producer), ERP 4.5% -> 9.7%, plus a 2.0pp country-risk premium = 11.7% cost of equity. Gross debt ~$1.0bn at ~7% (5% after tax) against a ~$13.4bn market cap pulls the blend to ~11.2%; WACC 11.0%. The CRP is deliberately about one-third of the production-weighted sovereign CRP (Cote d'Ivoire BB ~3.5pp, Burkina Faso and Senegal CCC+ ~9pp each, weighted ~6.5-7pp): revenue is USD gold sold offshore, cash is held offshore, and the remaining jurisdiction risk (mining-code fiscal creep, Burkina Faso convention renewals at Mana 2027 / Hounde 2029, higher withholding on upstreaming) is charged in the bear-scenario leakage rate and its 25% weight, not in the discount rate -- risk charged once, by category. The same WACC is used for all three scenarios. Expropriation of a currently operating mine (the Boungou/Wahgnion precedent applied to Hounde or Mana) is the tail this CRP covers.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. Lease principal ($32.6m FY2025, AR cash flow 21E) plus lease interest ($5.7m, AR p.9228) = $38m is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (0.7% of revenue, drifting to 0.6% as revenue grows), and lease liabilities ($88.8m at Dec-2025) are excluded from net debt. Mine D&A is almost entirely depletion of mining interests rather than right-of-use assets, so the da_pct_path is used unadjusted for cash tax.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged ONCE, in the flows. Host governments hold 10-20% free-carried interests in every mine (Ity 15%, Hounde 15%, Mana 15%, Sabodala-Massawa 10%, Lafigue 20%; Burkina Faso raised its stake from 10% to 15% in May 2025 under the 2024 code). FY2025 NCI share of net earnings was $209.9m (AR note 20) = 12.8% of EBIT, and NCI dividends paid were $119.1m. Rather than deduct the $383m book NCI (far below its economic value), cash_tax_rate_path is a COMBINED leakage rate on EBIT: income tax (FY2025 expense $454.2m = 27.7% of EBIT $1,638.5m; statutory 25% CI / 27.5% BF / 25% SN plus withholding on upstreaming) + NCI share 12.8% = 40.5%. Base uses 40%, bear 43% (fiscal creep), bull 39%. Calibration: FY2025 EBIT 1,638.5 x (1-0.405) = $975m vs adjusted net earnings attributable to shareholders $781.9m; the gap is finance costs (~$70m), the $265m realised hedge loss (below EBIT in the model's revenue basis, now rolled off) and FX -- within non-operating noise.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'), with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied: dual currency (USD flows / GBp quote), leases treatment B, NCI folded into leakage, risk charged once (CRP in WACC for expropriation tail; gold-price cyclicality and fiscal creep in the scenario flows). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. REVENUE IS BUILT AS OUNCES SOLD x GOLD PRICE, not from a historical CAGR -- gold is a commodity and the FY2020-25 revenue CAGR of 24% is mostly price. COMMODITY DECK: spot gold $4,220/oz (GC=F 2026-10-09 close; 52-week $3,901-5,586). The base case does NOT hold spot: it takes the FY2026 average at ~$4,390 (H1 realised $4,579 on ~560koz, H2 at spot on ~620koz), then normalises to $3,900 (FY2027), $3,500 (FY2028) and a $3,300/oz mid-cycle from FY2029 -- the company's own 2026 STIP planning price (AR p.6035) and roughly the 2024-26 trailing average -- inflating 1.5%/yr nominal thereafter (a real decline). Bear reverts to $2,600 by FY2029 (2024 realised $2,418 in 2029 dollars); bull holds spot ~$4,200 and inflates 2%/yr. COST FUNCTION calibrated to H1-2026 actuals (AISC $1,871 at $4,579; FY2026 AISC guidance $1,600-1,800 at $3,000; sustaining capex $280m): all-in cash cost ex sustaining capex (TCC incl. royalties + corporate + expensed exploration) = $1,520/oz at $3,000 gold, with a ~11% royalty slope on price above $3,000 (H1-2026 disclosed $184/oz royalty impact on $1,579/oz of price), inflating 2.5%/yr; Assafou enters from FY2029 at ~$950-1,050/oz all-in cash cost (DFS AISC $1,026 at $2,500). ebitda_margin_path is (price - cost)/price on the blended portfolio each year. VOLUMES: FY2026 1,180koz (guidance 1,090-1,265 midpoint; H1 564koz), FY2027 1,230, FY2028 1,260 (Sabodala-Massawa underground ramp, Mana declining), FY2029 1,430 (Assafou first full year, first gold H2-2028), FY2030 1,500 (company target), flat thereafter -- the +10yr mine-life target and the 12-15Moz 2026-30 discovery target are taken as replacing depletion but not growing beyond 1.5Moz. CAPEX: FY2026 $650m (280 sustaining + 270 non-sustaining + ~100 growth), FY2027-28 ~$1.05bn/yr (Assafou $1,061m upfront spread over the 24-30 month build plus underground development), FY2029 ~$680m, then ~13% of revenue (~$650m) which carries sustaining + non-sustaining stripping/reserve replacement. DEPLETION / TERMINAL: reserves 16.6Moz (~14 years at 1.2Moz) plus 20.7Moz M&I discovered since 2016; the terminal value at year 10 assumes reserve replacement continues at the modelled capex intensity, but the terminal cap is set at 10x FCF (below the 12-15x cyclical default) as the depletion haircut, and terminal growth is 1.5% (base/bear) / 2.0% (bull). FY2025 reported FCF ($1,133m) was depressed by $265m of realised revenue-protection settlements (hedge book rolled off in 2025) and a $244m working-capital build; on an unhedged basis owner FCF would have been ~$1.3bn, which is why the FY2026 Y1 FCF steps up to ~$1.5bn at a $4,390 average price. Working capital: -3% capture on the change in revenue (stockpiles and VAT receivables grow with activity; releases cash in the down years). Street basis: SBC is small (~1.2% of revenue) so the house/street band is narrow; band_position is computable.

commodity_assumptions.mid_cycle_rationale: $3,300/oz is Endeavour's own 2026 STIP planning price and close to the 2024-2026 realised average ($2,418 / $3,464 / ~$4,390). It sits ~22% below spot and ~40% below the 52-week high. Using spot in perpetuity would value a 1.5Moz producer at a margin no gold cycle has sustained; using the industry reserve price (~$2,000-2,200) would ignore five years of structural central-bank demand. The bear deck tests the 2013-style 30%+ correction; the bull deck is spot held in real terms.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case modelled 10-year revenue CAGR (mid-cycle gold price x volume path), not a historical CAGR -- for a single-commodity producer every trailing CAGR above is dominated by the gold price (FY2020 realised $1,761 -> FY2025 $3,464)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 8.1% diverges from revenue 24.4% and EPS 38.9% by far more than 30%: FY2021-24 carried $1.7bn of impairments and the Boungou/Wahgnion disposal losses, and the 3yr equity CAGR is negative (-6.1%) because of the $300m FY2024 loss and $288m FY2025 dividends. None of the trailing rates is used for projection.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income not stripped as net cash is immaterial): FY2020 494.3 -> FY2022 470.9 -> FY2025 1,068.6. Owner-FCF CAGRs (31.4% / 16.7%) are within 0.5pp of reported (31.0% / 17.2%) -- SBC is ~1.5% of revenue and not growing faster than cash flow; the 3yr figure is flattered by a depressed FY2022 base (hedge losses, Lafigue construction). EPS 3yr CAGR is undefined (FY2022 EPS -0.23).

base.narrative: Gold normalises from the FY2026 average (~$4,390) to a $3,300 mid-cycle by FY2029; volumes grow from 1,180koz to 1,500koz by 2030 as Sabodala-Massawa underground and Assafou (first gold H2-2028, 320koz/yr at ~$1,000 AISC) come on, then hold flat. Margin: 61.9% in FY2026 (H1 actual 62.5%) compressing to ~53% at $3,300 with cost inflation of 2.5%/yr partly offset by Assafou's low cost, then drifting down 0.5pp/yr as the price inflates slower than costs. Capex peaks at ~$1.05bn in FY2027-28 for the Assafou build, then ~13% of revenue. Combined tax + NCI leakage 40% of EBIT. Terminal: Gordon at 1.5% vs a 10x cap (depletion haircut).
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Combined income tax (~27%) + NCI free-carry share (~13%) on EBIT; see inputs.nci_treatment.

bull.narrative: Spot gold is the new floor: $4,450 FY2026 average easing only to $4,200 by FY2028 and then inflating 2%/yr (central-bank and ETF demand persist, real rates fall). Assafou delivers on the 5-for-5 build record, Sabodala-Massawa underground and the 2026-30 exploration programme take the group to 1,600koz by 2030 with Assafou's $1,026 AISC pulling the blended cost down to first quartile. Margins hold ~60-62% because royalty scaling is more than covered by price. Fiscal terms stable (39% leakage). Capex still carries the Assafou build in FY2027-28 then ~11.5% of revenue including continued growth spend.
bull.cash_tax_rate_note: Combined income tax + NCI leakage; 1pp below base for stable fiscal terms.

bear.narrative: A 2013-style correction: gold falls to $3,200 in FY2027 and $2,600-2,700 from FY2028 (still above the 2024 average in nominal terms) while the cost base inflates 2.5%/yr and the royalty relief below $3,000 is small. Production sits at the low end of guidance (1,150koz) and Assafou -- committed at FID end-2026 before the price falls -- is built on budget but ramps a year late, so FY2027-28 capex of ~$1.0bn lands on $3.2-3.8bn of revenue and FCF is near zero in FY2028. Fiscal creep: Burkina Faso's 2024 code applies at the Mana (2027) and Hounde (2029) convention renewals, Cote d'Ivoire's new code raises the state share, and withholding on upstreaming rises -- combined leakage 43%. Margins compress to ~40% and drift lower. The shareholder-returns programme's $3,000/oz condition fails. Expropriation of an operating mine is NOT in this path; it is the tail the WACC country premium covers.
bear.cash_tax_rate_note: Combined income tax + NCI leakage rising to 43% on mining-code fiscal creep.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle gold at $3,300 from FY2029 after a two-year glide from today's ~$4,400 average; 1.5Moz by 2030 on Sabodala-Massawa underground plus Assafou on schedule; margins ~53% at mid-cycle; Assafou build capex peaks FY2027-28; combined tax+NCI leakage 40%; WACC 11% with a 2pp West Africa premium; 10x terminal cap for depletion.
scenario_narratives.bull: Spot gold (~$4,200+) persists and inflates; Assafou and exploration take the group to 1.6Moz at first-quartile cost; margins hold 60%+; fiscal terms stable. The axes that must BOTH go right are the gold price and project/exploration delivery.
scenario_narratives.bear: Gold corrects to $2,600-2,700 by FY2028 just as the Assafou build consumes ~$1bn of capex; cost inflation and Sahel fiscal creep (Burkina Faso code renewals, higher state take) compress margins to ~40%; production stalls at 1.15-1.35Moz; returns programme suspended. Nationalisation of an operating mine is excluded from the flows and charged in the WACC premium instead.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% and bull cut from 35% to 25%. Gold at ~$4,200 is near twice its 2024 average and the historical pattern after spikes of this size (1980, 2011-13) is mean reversion, so the price distribution around spot is at best symmetric rather than bull-skewed; and ~34-39% of production is in Burkina Faso under a military government whose 2024 code has already lifted the state's free carry and whose convention renewals fall inside the forecast window. The bull case needs two independent things -- gold holding spot AND Assafou/exploration delivering 1.6Moz -- so it does not earn the compounder default of 35%. Base keeps 50%: guidance has been met or beaten in 12 of 13 years and the balance sheet (net cash, $1.2bn liquidity) means no scenario involves solvency stress.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A gold miner is a leveraged, depleting claim on a commodity price. The house value therefore (1) builds revenue from ounces x a gold deck that normalises to a defensible mid-cycle price rather than extrapolating spot, (2) calibrates the cost base to the latest actual AISC and the royalty slope that makes AISC rise with price, (3) charges host-government free carries and taxes as one leakage rate on EBIT, (4) prices the Sahel expropriation tail once, in a 2pp country premium on an 11% USD WACC, and (5) treats the terminal as a depleting asset with a 10x FCF cap. The three scenarios are gold-price regimes with their matching volume, cost and fiscal paths; the result is probability-weighted at 25/50/25. On these inputs the shares trade modestly above the house weighted value: the market is pricing a long-run gold price of roughly $3,800-4,000 or a lower discount rate than the jurisdiction warrants.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gold price: every $100/oz on the long-run deck moves base-case annual FCF by ~$90m after royalties and leakage, roughly $2.5-3/share (190-230p) of value; the bull-bear spread is almost entirely the gold deck

Burkina Faso (~34-39% of production, CCC+ sovereign): Mana convention renewal 2027 and Hounde 2029 under the 2024 code; the Boungou/Wahgnion nationalisation precedent -- an outright loss of Hounde would remove ~24% of revenue and is only in the WACC premium, not the flows
Assafou execution: $1,061m upfront capital (-10/+15%) over 2027-28; a 12-month delay or 15% overrun costs ~$1-1.5/share; FID expected by year-end 2026

Cost inflation and royalty scaling: FY2026 AISC guidance of $1,600-1,800 is 12-25% above FY2025 actual; the model's 2.5%/yr inflation and 11% royalty slope are calibrated to H1-2026 and could prove light if the CFA/euro strengthens further against the USD
Reserve replacement: the flat 1.5Moz terminal assumes the 12-15Moz 2026-30 discovery target replaces depletion; failure would shorten the tail the 10x cap already discounts
Timing convention: Y1 (FY2026) is discounted a full year from a notional January start and H1-2026 FCF is inside both Y1 and the June net-cash anchor; net effect is conservative by a few percent
